title: St. Louis on the way home and its piano players
summary: On the trip back he played in Bailey's place in St. Louis for several nights, found better musicians there than in Chicago, and compares pianists everywhere to jukeboxes.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: picked up about five or six dollars around there and I got that little change and I hoboed my way had enough to buy enough food to come on down and I hoboed my way all the way from Chicago back here took me about six days to do it but I done it, I come on back I was in St. Louis I played I was playing the Beale Street Blues then when I was in I played the Beale Street Blues, I played the Yardin' Down Blues in St. Louis it was in old man's place that old gray man up there, they called Bailey, I played in his place about four or five nights in St. Louis and I left there I left St. Louis there was nothing more than that, it looked like I couldn't make nothing there and I come on back tips wasn't so good then I didn't left there and come on back see the boats of the places that you'd be playing they wouldn't hire so they wasn't getting no siren so you just had to figure out what you'd pick up around
did you hear any good ragtime players in St. Louis?

oh yeah they had plenty of good musicians there and so the fact they had better musicians in St. Louis at that time than they had in Chicago it was jazz music yeah they had better ones in St. Louis than they had in Chicago stuff stuff stuff

around Mark Street, there was a, I remember there was being some kind of a ballroom or cabaret there. The man had piano players around about a thousand. Yeah, there had piano players around about a thousand. They say it in your head. They say piano players. They say piano in your head was there. That was no trouble about a piano player. They say, well, I can't do it. You didn't have to, you didn't have to do a trumpet if I had to play. You could, this go up most of any corner and you could find somebody who could play. That's how I tell you, when the jukebox started coming in, they started putting the jukebox on the corner playing for nickel. It's the same way as when organ grinding was coming around. The big house party would be going on. And organ grinding would get on the corner and grind that organ and play it. Everybody run out the party and organ playing. Yeah, I played organ. On the corner. That's how that goes. It wasn't that.
